transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11 14:00 UTC  | Duration: ~49 minutes  | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Sofia (CSM), Liam (SE) - Redwood; Priya (Head ML Ops), Marco (CTO), Daniel (PM), Eva (Finance) - Aventum

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: Priya here.
[00:07] Marco: Marco on.
[00:09] Daniel: Daniel.
[00:12] Eva: Eva.
[00:14] Sofia: Sofia, good to be here.
[00:15] Liam: Liam here.
[00:18] Jared: Cool. Agenda — run through the usage spike we saw last week, cost impact, a short ops checklist for the personalization-v2 rollout, and next steps on procurement / runway. Sound right?
[00:29] Priya: Yep, that's what we need. The spike caught us off guard.

[02:10] Daniel: Quick context for the group — we pushed personalization-v2 to canary on Tuesday. It's live at 10% traffic for recommendations. We saw token burn jump, and latency for long prompt sessions increased from ~120ms median to about 210ms, so that added to costs.
[02:33] Liam: I'm seeing the trace — looks like longer decode windows + KV cache thrashing for sessions where users have long histories. The K-V cache (transcribed in logs as K V cash) gets churned because of prefix variance. We recommended prefix normalization in the design doc, did you implement that?
[02:55] Priya: We did partial normalization but not complete. Time pressure got to us.
[03:07] Jared: Ok. Two tracks as I see it: quick-mitigations to reduce immediate burn, and medium-term config changes to stabilize cost and latency. Quick things: enable aggressive prefix caching on the personalization endpoint, reduce max_generation tokens on non-critical calls, and fall back to a quantized model for tail traffic.
[04:01] Eva: Quantized variant sounds good but what's the expected quality delta? Finance wants to see exact numbers before approving budget reallocation.
[04:12] Sofia: We'll provide an A/B eval sample — historically our quantized 4-bit on similar autoregressive models had ~1-2% drop on rerank accuracy for recommendation tasks, often imperceptible in production. But we should test that on your eval set.
[04:31] Marco: Also curious about Dedicated capacity. If we do a reserved pool, will that reduce unit cost enough to justify procurement? Our CFO is asking for a delta analysis.
[04:45] Jared: Yes. Basic math: reserved Dedicated reduces per-token compute cost ~20-35% depending on commit size and GPU generation. We'll put together a 6 month vs hosted scenario. Sofia?
[04:58] Sofia: I'll model two scenarios: (A) keep hosted and apply caching/quantization, (B) commit to a mid-sized Dedicated pool with autoscale and burst. I'll include sensitivity for continued traffic growth.

[06:20] Daniel: On the latency front — users report tail latency spikes during peak. Is that pure queuing or model frag?
[06:28] Liam: Mostly queue + scheduling. Our runtime's continuous batching tries to maximize throughput; during spikes, long sequences block some GPU slots causing head-of-line latencies. We can lower batching window for that endpoint to favor latency at cost of some throughput efficiency.
[06:44] Priya: Can we do dynamic routing — keep hot-critical routes at low latency profile and cheaper routes for async tasks?
[06:52] Jared: Exactly, smart routing can direct session-based recommendations to low-latency profile and background batch scoring to cheaper quantized pools. We'll share routing policy templates.

[09:10] Eva: Ok finance question — what's the absolute worst case token burn over a 7-day window if traffic spikes like last week? We need a high-water mark for runway planning.
[09:22] Liam: I can pull a 7-day burn report and highlight the top 5 most expensive endpoints. It will include per-route median latency, tokens per call, and cost per thousand tokens.
[09:35] Jared: We'll also annotate any anomalies — e.g., test traffic or misconfigured retry loops — that inflated numbers. In your case, I suspect higher retry loops from client side contributed.

[11:03] Priya: There was a bug in the client that retried on 502; fixed now. But that did increase both calls and token counts.
[11:12] Marco: Good catch. We need better guardrails. Can Redwood emit alerts when per-route tokens exceed a threshold?
[11:20] Sofia: Yes, we have token-level alerts, and cost anomalies. We can propose two alert tiers: notifier to the ML team, and an automatic throttle when cost per minute crosses X. We'll propose thresholds.

[13:00] Daniel: On security/compliance, procurement asked for KMS integration details and audit log retention. Last QBR said 90 days of audit logs is default. We need 12 months for internal compliance. Is that doable?
[13:12] Jared: For hosted, we can push logs to your SIEM via our export connector; retention is configurable as a paid add-on. For Private deployments you'll manage retention directly. KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and also integrations with HSM — we can attach the one-pager.
[13:33] Priya: For the pilot we want SSO + RBAC enforced, plus just-in-time access for developers.
[13:39] Liam: SSO SAML is supported; RBAC granular roles for model / route management are available. We can demo permission flows.

[16:45] Marco: Procurement timeline — if we opt for Dedicated, procurement lead time is about 6 weeks. Can Redwood fast-track an onboarding so we can start canary tests before procurement completes?
[16:58] Jared: Yes. Two options: start pilot on hosted with canary traffic, then snapshot configs for Dedicated; or purchase a short trial Dedicated for 30 days while procurement loops. We often do short trial bursts for enterprise pilots. I'll flag that.

[19:02] Eva: From finance side, we need an explicit delta for committed vs hosted to present to CFO. Please include predictable TCO assumptions and break-even as function of sustained qps.
[19:14] Sofia: Will do. I'll create an excel with scenarios: base case (current usage), spike case (1.8x), and sustained growth (3x). Each will include reserved discount tiers.

[21:22] Daniel: Regarding the canary plan for personalization-v2 — our PM goal is to ramp from 10% to 50% across 4 weeks if metrics hold. We need gating criteria.
[21:34] Liam: Typical gates: 1) latency median and 95th under threshold; 2) quality regression below X% on rerank metrics; 3) error rate below 0.2%. We'll instrument evals and production checks.
[21:50] Priya: We also want a rollback policy — automatic fallback to prior model if errors or cost blowouts exceed thresholds.
[21:58] Jared: Redwood supports canary rollbacks and auto-fallback policies. We can configure a circuit-breaker: if 5-minute rolling cost exceeds baseline by 40% or error rate > threshold, traffic auto-redirects to previous version.

[24:05] Marco: How much visibility will we have in the console? Can we see token-level breakdowns per user session?
[24:14] Sofia: Yes — token-level samples are available, with per-session grouping. PII is redacted by default, but you can request deeper traces for debugging under a support ticket.

[26:30] Priya: On instrumentation: we need a daily digest for the core ML team highlighting anomalies and top cost contributors. Is that something Redwood can send?
[26:39] Sofia: Yes — we'll set up a daily digest email and link to the dashboard. We can also push to your Slack #ml-ops channel for high severity.

[28:50] Eva: A question about credits — are there any onboarding credits for committed pilots?
[28:57] Jared: We sometimes apply pilot credits, and there's a program for mid-size pilots that offset initial Dedicated commit. I'll include potential credit amounts in the pricing doc.

[31:05] Daniel: Are we tracking any open technical debt that could bite us later? The team discovered inconsistent prompt templates across clients which increases token usage.
[31:18] Priya: Yeah, that's on us. We're planning a prompt standardization sprint. But is there a tooling way to reject oversized prompts before they reach the model?
[31:29] Liam: We can do pre-request middleware that enforces prompt size limits and warns clients. Redwood supports route-level max_token configurations and can reject or truncate.

[33:10] Marco: For the sake of the board update, can we get a one-page executive summary: current run-rate, worst-case 7-day burn, mitigation plan, and cost delta if we commit?
[33:21] Jared: Yes — we'll produce an exec summary PDF. Expect it in the follow-up email.

[35:44] Sofia: Quick note on performance tuning — we have two knob sets: batching/latency and quantization profiles. For personalization, I recommend a mixed pool: lower-latency model for interactive sessions and a quantized copy for background scoring. That gives best compromise.
[35:59] Priya: How disruptive is switching traffic between variants?
[36:04] Liam: Seamless from routing perspective; metrics and cache warming are the main issues. We'll warm KV caches with a synthetic warmup run. There may be a short blip in tail latency when switching large percentages of traffic.

[38:20] Eva: If we do a 6-month commit, do we get a fixed rate for the period?
[38:26] Jared: Yes, pricing can be fixed for the duration of the commit. We'll include that in the pricing scenario. Also note there's a cancellation uplift clause if usage falls below commit thresholds.

[40:00] Daniel: A bit of housekeeping: can Redwood include a short sample alert configuration in the follow-up for our on-call playbook?
[40:08] Sofia: Absolutely. We'll include sample playbook snippets (PagerDuty + Slack + email).

[42:12] Priya: One operational ask: during the canary we want to keep more detailed audit logs for just the canary window (30 days) but we don't want that retained forever. Can Redwood support temporary elevated retention?
[42:24] Liam: Yes — you can set route-level retention policies. We'll show how to toggle retention for the canary window.

[44:30] Jared: Great. Let's recap next steps quickly.
[44:36] Sofia: I'll prepare pricing scenarios and the alert/playbook snips.
[44:40] Liam: I'll share the 7-day burn dashboard and the canary warmup plan.
[44:45] Jared: I'll include SOC2/KMS one-pager, pilot credit options, and the exec summary PDF.
[44:52] Priya: I'll confirm canary stakeholders and provide test datasets.
[44:56] Eva: I'll get back with budget decision by Friday 2026-04-16.

[46:10] Jared: Anything else?
[46:14] Marco: No, thanks all.
[46:17] Daniel: Thanks.
[46:19] Sofia: Thanks, everyone.
[46:22] Priya: Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript contains natural disfluencies and occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K-V cash). Action items captured above. Follow-up email to contain: 7-day burn dashboard link, pricing scenarios, SOC2/KMS one-pager, alert config snippets, canary warmup runbook, and credit options.
